title: Holbeck Foods — a lakehouse that costs too much and trusts too little

tabs.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Holbeck Foods supplies supermarkets from eleven distribution centres. An Azure Databricks lakehouse feeds demand forecasting and a nightly replenishment run, built over two years by a team that has since changed entirely.
Finance has queried the platform bill and the forecasting team has stopped trusting the silver layer. The findings below came out of a review of both complaints.

tabs.heading: Existing environment
paragraphs: Every scheduled job runs on an all-purpose cluster that a previous engineer created and left running with no auto-termination. It has been up continuously for seven months.

Order files land in an ADLS Gen2 container throughout the day, roughly forty thousand small JSON files a week. The current notebook lists the whole directory on each run and reprocesses anything whose modified date is recent, which has begun to miss files and occasionally duplicate them.

The silver orders table is partitioned by order_id. There are 14 million distinct values. Queries filtering on distribution centre and date are slow, and the table directory contains an enormous number of very small files.

A supplier dimension is maintained with an overwrite on every run. The forecasting team needs to know what a supplier's category and lead time were at the time of a historical order, and that information no longer exists anywhere.

Rows with null quantities reach the gold aggregates and produce understated forecasts. There is no validation anywhere in the pipeline; the problem is found by a planner noticing a number looks wrong.

One nightly Spark job has a stage where a single task runs for fifty minutes while its 199 peers finish in under a minute. The cluster was doubled in size last month and the stage took the same fifty minutes.

tabs.heading: Requirements
paragraphs: Scheduled work must stop running on a permanently live interactive cluster.
File ingestion must process each new file exactly once without listing the whole directory each run.
The silver orders table must be laid out so that filters on distribution centre and date are fast, without committing to a partitioning scheme that cannot later be changed.
The supplier dimension must record what each attribute was at any past point in time.
Rows with null quantities must be prevented from reaching the gold layer, and the pipeline must report how many were rejected.
The fifty-minute stage must be diagnosed correctly, given that adding compute changed nothing.
